title: Deployment Sherpa — Field Guide + Calendar (Sep 2026, WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a light-weight, human-first guide for shepherding the September 2026 service update. The "Sherpa" metaphor is intentional: we want a small core team to guide the change, reduce cognitive load for engineers in the valley (users), and set clear summit windows and bailout routes.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- A compact pre-flight checklist emphasizing telemetry gates and thin rollback slices.
- A 7-day calendar around the summit window showing who does what, with exact handover times.
- A small decision-tree for go/no-go calls and escalation links.
- Communication templates for customer- and internal-facing notes.
- Open questions and follow-ups for the next planning sync.

High-level timeline (summit weekend):
- Basecamp prep (Mon–Tue): config freezes, test sweep, smoke scenarios deployed to canaries.
- Sherpa window (Wed–Thu): staggered lane increases, 30m observation cycles.
- Summit window (Fri 02:00–08:00 UTC): primary push to 100% of the non-dedicated tier.
- Descent (Fri 08:00–Tue): telemetry sampling and polish, roll-forwards for minor regressions.

Roles + contacts (primary Sherpa roster):
- Sherpa Lead: Maya Chen — overall conductor (pager: maya, slack: #sherpa-lead)
- Traffic Sherpa: Liam O'Rourke — routing, throttles, and traffic shaping
- Runtime Sherpa: Priya Nair — model-serving runtime and kernel fallback
- Observability Sherpa: Carlos Mejia — metrics/trace lead and canary gates
- Customer Liaison: Zoe Patel — status updates, CS triage, and postmortem owner
- On-call backup: eng-sre rotation (see linked roster in Confluence)

Pre-flight checklist (quick read, run this twice before summit window):
- Config hygiene
  - Confirm feature flags for new shard routing are off in prod until Sherpa window (FF-9876).
  - Pin model version MR-2026-09-18 in deployment manifests for canaries.
- Testing sweep
  - Canary smoke: run 6 synthetic prompts including long-sequence and KV-cache bust.
  - Load test: 30m 2x baseline to validate autoscaler thresholds.
- Observability
  - Dashboards: latest nightly-telemetry saved and shared with Sherpa team.
  - Alerts: ensure severity mapping for latency spike, increased 5xx, and token-cost regressions.
- Rollback readiness
  - Artifacts: previous stable image tagged and accessible (image: redwood/inference:v2026-09-02-stable).
  - Rollback runbook: one-click rollback test on staging executed successfully.
- Communication
  - Draft external status page message (pre-announce + in-window template) in this doc.
  - Slack channels created and pinned (e.g., #sherpa-2026-09-10).

Observation cycles (Sherpa cadence):
- Cadence length: 30 minutes for the first 3 hours after each major ramp; can relax to 60 minutes after 12h of stability.
- During each cycle capture: p95 latency, tail latency (>99), 5xx rate, model output-quality quick check (3 sample prompts), cost per token metric.
- Decision inputs: if any gate crosses threshold (see gates table) hold ramp and escalate to Runtime Sherpa.

Telemetry gates (fast-fail thresholds — trigger immediate hold/rollback):
- p95 latency increases >30% vs last 24h baseline for two consecutive cycles -> HOLD
- 5xx rate >0.5% sustained over a 15-minute window -> HOLD and page eng-sre
- Token-cost/unit increase >25% over baseline without corresponding quality improvement -> PAUSE and investigate
- Quality regressions (human-evaluated failed prompts >=2/3 sampled checks) -> PAUSE and rollback candidate

Decision tree (succinct):
1) Preflight checks green? No -> stop and fix. Yes -> proceed to Sherpa window.
2) During ramp, gate triggered? Yes -> hold ramp, notify channel, run mitigations from mitigation matrix.
3) Mitigation resolves within 60 minutes? Yes -> resume at previous stable %. No -> consider rollback to pinned artifact.
4) Post-rollback stability verified for 30 minutes? Yes -> re-plan smaller rollout. No -> page incident commander and open incident timeline.

Rollback slices (preferred order of actions to reduce blast radius):
- Step 0: Pause traffic.
- Step 1: Route traffic to previous model variant (weight-based shift: 80/20, 100 within 10m).
- Step 2: If model variant route not available, redeploy stable image to the smallest affected pool first (canary pool), validate then scale back up.
- Step 3: If no quick redeploy possible, shift traffic to Dedicated pool (if customer-tiered) and slow down host autoscaling.

Communication templates (short):
- Internal (Slack pinned): "[SHERPA] Summit window in progress — holding at 40% traffic due to p95 delta. Mentioning @runtime-sherpa for mitigation. More updates every 30m."
- External (Status page): "We are deploying an update to inference routing. Some requests may see slight latency increases during the maintenance window (Fri 02:00–08:00 UTC). We will post status updates on the page if disruptions occur."
- Customer message (for impacted enterprise): "Quick note — we detected anomalous tail latency on a small subset during today's rollout and paused. Our engineers are remediating; expect a follow-up within 60 minutes. — Zoe P., Customer Ops"

7-day micro-calendar (example days around the summit):
- Mon 2026-09-06: Basecamp prep. Config freeze 17:00 UTC. Smoke suite run and results posted.
- Tue 2026-09-07: Canary roll to 2% across region-north and region-eu. Observability Sherpa validates trace patterns.
- Wed 2026-09-08: Ramp to 25% in lanes with short session. 30m cycles until midnight.
- Thu 2026-09-09: Ramp to 60%. Warm-up caches and KV rehydration checks.
- Fri 2026-09-10 (Summit): 02:00 UTC begin final ramp; expected 100% non-dedicated by 06:00 UTC. Sherpa rota covers 00:00–12:00 UTC.
- Sat 2026-09-11: Low-key monitoring, optional rollback window for enterprise customers.
- Sun 2026-09-12: Post-deployment metrics summary drafted and shared with leadership.

Handover notes and shift transitions:
- Handover format (5 bullets): current % coverage, active mitigations, outstanding alerts, open PRs related to deployment, next check-in timestamp.
- Handover boundary must always include a clear go/no-go state and whether rollback artifacts are staged.

Quick cheat sheet (one-liners):
- If latency spike + 5xx spike at same time -> assume runtime kernel regression; page Runtime Sherpa.
- If costs spike with stable latency -> suspect quantization/telemetry mislabel; pause throttles and investigate cost table.
- If only a small demographic reports quality issues -> consider targeted rollback to variant.

Open questions / TODOs (action items before next planning sync):
- [ ] Confirm Dedicated pool routing failover plan with infra (action: Liam).
- [ ] Add autoscaler synthetic that simulates KV-cache warmup (action: Priya).
- [ ] Finalize external status language for enterprise customers (action: Zoe).
- [ ] Run a dry-run rollback on staging with the live traffic simulator (action: eng-sre).

Notes to self (choppy, rough):
- Remember to pin telemetry snapshot before each ramp.
- Consider keeping a small color-coded whiteboard in the monitor room for live status updates.
- Possible follow-up: create a condensed one-page "Sherpa crib sheet" for on-call pockets.

Postmortem anchors (if incident occurs):
- Timeline: mm:ss-level events captured into incident doc.
- Owners: who executed which step and when.
- Signal loss analysis: which gate failed first and what was root cause.
- Remediation: hotfix vs design fix and time-to-complete.

Appendix: handy links and ids
- Confluence runbook: https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/ENG/Deployment+Playbooks
- Incident template: https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/ENG/Incident+Template
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4567

End of doc — keep this intentionally lean. Add comments inline below in future edits.
summary: Compact field guide for Sept 2026 deployment: roles, checklists, telemetry gates, 7-day calendar, decision tree, rollback slices, communication templates, open actions.
